extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of affected electric generating units (EGUs), designated representatives, environmental compliance managers, and permitting/monitoring personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and procedures for monitoring, calculating, reporting, recordkeeping, and demonstrating compliance with EPA CO2 emission standards for affected EGUs (steam generating units, stationary combustion turbines, IGCC, CHP, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emission limit for modified steam generating units
rubrics_metrics.description: For modified steam generating units, you must not discharge from the affected EGU any gases that contain CO2 in excess of 230 lb CO2/MMBtu.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring plan requirement and submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a monitoring plan to quantify the hourly CO2 mass emission rate (tons/h) in accordance with 40 CFR 75.53(g) and (h). The electronic portion must be submitted using the ECMPS Client Tool and must be in place prior to reporting emissions data and/or monitoring system certification tests. Monitoring plan must be updated as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring plan submittals must be made by the Designated Representative (DR), the Alternate DR, or a delegated agent (see §60.5555a(d) and (e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Combustion turbine limited applicability and fuel-records requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Combustion turbines qualifying under §60.5520a(d)(1) are not subject to this section other than the requirement to maintain fuel purchase records for permitted fuel(s). If a combustion turbine uses non-uniform fuels under §60.5520a(d)(2), must monitor heat input per paragraph (c)(1) and monitor CO2 per paragraph (b) or (c).

rubrics_metrics.name: General requirement to determine hourly CO2 mass emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: You must determine the hourly CO2 mass emissions in kg from your affected EGU(s) according to paragraphs (b)(1) through (5) of this section, or if applicable, as provided in paragraph (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies choice of direct-monitoring approaches (CEMS) or alternative fuel/heat-input based calculation methodologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEMS installation and alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: For an affected EGU that combusts coal you must, and for all other affected EGUs you may, install, certify, operate, maintain, and calibrate a CO2 continuous emission monitoring system (CEMS) to directly measure and record hourly average CO2 concentrations, and a flow monitoring system per 40 CFR 75.10(a)(3)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As an alternative to direct CO2 concentration measurement, provided the EGU does not use carbon separation, you may use data from a certified O2 monitor to calculate hourly average CO2 concentrations per 40 CFR 75.10(a)(3)(iii). If CO2 concentration is measured on a dry basis you must also install and maintain a continuous moisture monitoring system per 40 CFR 75.11(b), or use an appropriate fuel-specific default moisture value from 75.11(b) or petition for a site-specific default per 40 CFR 75.66.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification and QA procedures for monitoring systems
rubrics_metrics.description: For each continuous monitoring system used to determine CO2 mass emissions, you must meet the applicable certification and quality assurance procedures in 40 CFR 75.20 and appendices A and B to 40 CFR part 75.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of unadjusted exhaust gas volumetric flow rates
rubrics_metrics.description: You must use only unadjusted exhaust gas volumetric flow rates to determine the hourly CO2 mass emissions rate from the affected EGU; you must not apply the bias adjustment factors described in Section 7.6.5 of appendix A to 40 CFR part 75 to the exhaust gas flow rate data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow monitor setup and RATA reference method selection
rubrics_metrics.description: You must select an appropriate reference method to set up (characterize) the flow monitor and to perform the on-going RATAs, in accordance with 40 CFR part 75.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you use a Type-S pitot tube or pitot tube assembly for the flow RATAs, you must calibrate the pitot tube or assembly and may not use the 0.84 default Type-S pitot tube coefficient specified in Method 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation steps for hourly CO2 mass emissions (valid operating hours)
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate the hourly CO2 mass emissions (kg) as described in paragraphs (b)(5)(i) through (iv). Perform this calculation only for “valid operating hours” as defined in §60.5540(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (i) Begin with the hourly CO2 mass emission rate (tons/h) from Equation F-11 in appendix F (wet basis) or procedure in section 4.2 of appendix F (dry basis). (ii) Multiply hourly tons/h by EGU or stack operating time (hours) to get tons CO2. (iii) Multiply by 907.2 to convert tons to kg and round to nearest kg. (iv) Hourly CO2 tons/h and operating times must be recorded under 40 CFR 75.57(e) and reported electronically under 40 CFR 75.64(a)(6). Use these data to calculate hourly CO2 mass emissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative heat-input-based monitoring for liquid/gaseous fuels
rubrics_metrics.description: If your affected EGU exclusively combusts liquid and/or gaseous fuel, as an alternative to paragraph (b) you may determine hourly CO2 mass emissions per paragraphs (c)(1) through (4) (heat-input-based procedures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1) Implement appendix D to 40 CFR part 75 procedures to determine hourly heat input rates (MMBtu/h) based on fuel flow and periodic GCV determinations. (2) Use Equation G-4 in appendix G to calculate hourly CO2 mass emission rate (tons/h). You may determine site-specific carbon-based F-factors using Equation F-7b and use them instead of default Fc values. (3) For each valid operating hour multiply tons/h by operating time and convert to kg; round to nearest two significant figures. (4) Hourly tons/h and operating times must be recorded under 75.57(e) and reported under 75.64(a)(6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative procedures for turbines firing non-uniform fuels
rubrics_metrics.description: If you operate a combustion turbine firing non-uniform fuels, you may determine CO2 emissions during the compliance period using one of: (i) units firing fuel gas follow §60.107a(d) and convert heat input to CO2 using Eq G-4; (ii) use Tier 3 methodology under 40 CFR 98.33(a)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining basis of emissions standard — output-based metering
rubrics_metrics.description: If you operate a source subject to an output-based standard (e.g., lb CO2 per gross or net MWh), you must install, calibrate, maintain, and operate watt meters to continuously measure and record hourly gross or net electric output using 0.2 class electricity metering instrumentation and calibration procedures per ANSI No. C12.20-2010.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For CHP EGUs also install/operate meters to continuously determine and record total useful thermal output hour-by-hour. For process steam applications install meters to continuously determine and record hourly steam flow rate, temperature, and pressure. Ensure plan covers installation/calibration/maintenance of all components used in the determination hour-by-hour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining basis of emissions standard — heat-input-based with non-uniform fuels
rubrics_metrics.description: If you operate a source subject to a heat-input-based standard and use non-uniform heating value fuels as in §60.5520a(d), you must determine total heat input for each fuel during the compliance period using one of: appendix D to 40 CFR part 75; §60.107a(d) procedures; or, if monitoring CO2 per Tier 3 methodology under 40 CFR 98.33(a)(3), convert CO2 to heat input using table C-1 of 40 CFR part 98 or determine fuel-specific Fc per Method 19 and convert using Eq G-4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apportionment when multiple EGUs serve a common electric generator
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more affected EGUs serve a common electric generator, apportion the combined hourly gross or net energy output to individual EGUs according to fraction of total steam load and/or direct mechanical energy contributed, or if identical EGUs apportion by fraction of total heat input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatively, you may propose alternate apportionment methods and provide information satisfactory to the Administrator; the Administrator may approve alternate methods if they ensure accurate estimation of emissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring options when EGUs share a common exhaust gas stack
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more affected EGUs that implement continuous emission monitoring share a common exhaust gas stack you must monitor hourly CO2 mass emissions in accordance with one of: (1) monitor the common stack if EGUs are subject to the same emissions standard in table 1 and express operating time as “stack operating hours”; or (2) monitor each EGU separately prior to mixing or apportion emissions based on unit load contribution and F-factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If monitoring common stack and compliance attained at stack, each affected EGU sharing the stack is in compliance. Administrator may approve alternate apportionment methods that ensure accurate estimation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring where exhaust gases are emitted through multiple stacks/ducts
rubrics_metrics.description: If exhaust gases are emitted through multiple stacks or routed through multiple ducts and you elect to monitor in ducts, you must monitor hourly CO2 mass emissions and stack operating time at each stack or duct separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine compliance by summing CO2 mass emissions measured at individual stacks/ducts and dividing by total gross or net energy output for the affected EGU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valid operating hours and exclusions for compliance periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Each compliance period shall include only “valid operating hours”, i.e., hours for which (i) “valid data” are obtained for all parameters used to determine hourly CO2 mass emissions (and heat input if applicable), and (ii) corresponding hourly gross or net energy output value is valid data (zero is valid for hours with no useful output).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude hours in which (i) part 75 substitute data provisions are applied for any parameter used to determine emissions/heat input, (ii) an exceedance of the full-scale range of a CEMS occurs for any parameters used, or (iii) total gross/net energy output or total heat input is unavailable. At least 95% of operating hours in the compliance period must be valid operating hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of total CO2 mass emissions for compliance period
rubrics_metrics.description: You must calculate the total CO2 mass emissions by summing the valid hourly CO2 mass emissions values from §60.5535a for all valid operating hours in the compliance period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of hourly gross/net energy output (P_gross/net)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each valid operating hour used in the total CO2 calculation you must determine P_gross/net (hourly gross or net energy output in MWh) according to procedures in paragraphs (a)(5)(i) and (ii), using the provided equation and components (Pe_ST, Pe_CT, Pe_IE, Pe_FW, Pe_A, Pt_PS, Pt_HR, Pt_IE, and TDF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert each hourly gross/net energy output value reported under part 75 by multiplying by the corresponding EGU or stack operating time. For CHP calculate Pt_PS per Equation 2 using measured useful thermal output flow (Qm), enthalpy (H), and conversion factors. TDF = 0.95 for CHP meeting thermal output threshold, 1.0 for others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of emissions rate and rounding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If subject to an output-based standard, calculate CO2 mass emissions rate (kg/MWh) by dividing total CO2 mass emissions by total gross or net energy output for compliance period. If subject to heat-input-based standard, divide total CO2 mass emissions by total heat input (kg/GJ or lb/MMBtu).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Round result to two significant figures if <1,000; three significant figures if >1,000. For heat-input-based standards round to two significant figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for system emergency and emergency standards
rubrics_metrics.description: You may exclude CO2 mass emissions and output generated from your affected EGU for hours operated during a system emergency (as defined in §60.5580a) if you can provide the information listed in §60.5560a(i). While operating during a system emergency, compliance depends on subcategory/unit type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For intermediate or base load combustion turbines the CO2 emission standard during system emergency is the applicable emission standard for low load combustion turbines. For affected modified steam generating units the emergency standard is 230 lb CO2/MMBtu.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall compliance demonstration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For the initial and each subsequent 12-operating-month compliance period, the CO2 mass emissions rate for your affected EGU must be determined per the specified procedures and must be less than or equal to the applicable CO2 emissions standard in table 1 to this subpart, or the emissions standard calculated under §60.5525a(a)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: One-time compliance date extension for new/reconstructed turbines installing add-on controls
rubrics_metrics.description: New or reconstructed stationary combustion turbines in the base load subcategory installing add-on controls that cannot comply with the Phase 2 CO2 standard by Jan 1, 2032 due to circumstances beyond control may request a compliance date extension of no longer than one year beyond Jan 1, 2032, and may only receive an extension once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extension request must contain a demonstration of necessity that: identifies affected units and controls; describes progress toward installation (contracts, permits); identifies circumstances beyond control (vendor info, permit delays, infrastructure delays); and proposes a compliance date no later than one year after the applicable compliance date. Submit all documentation no later than 6 months prior to applicable effective date and notify Administrator at time of submission. Administrator approves/disapproves based on written determination that required demonstrations and documentation were provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notifications to submit and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: You must prepare and submit the notifications specified in §§60.7(a)(1) and (3) and 60.19, as applicable to your affected EGUs (see table 3 to this subpart), and prepare and submit notifications specified in 40 CFR 75.61, as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterly electronic reporting schedule for 12-month rolling-average units
rubrics_metrics.description: For EGUs required to conduct initial and ongoing compliance determinations on a 12-operating-month rolling average basis, submit electronic quarterly reports: after first 12 months submit the calendar quarter report that includes the twelfth month no later than 30 days after end of that quarter; thereafter submit a report for each subsequent quarter no later than 30 days after quarter end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterly report content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each quarterly report must include, as applicable: (i) each rolling average CO2 mass emissions rate for which the last (twelfth) operating month falls within the calendar quarter (calculated per §60.5540a) and the dates of first and twelfth months; (ii) identification of each operating month in the quarter where the EGU violated the applicable CO2 standard; (iii) statement if no violations in any compliance periods ending in the quarter; (iv) percentage of valid operating hours in each 12-operating-month compliance period; (v) the CO2 emissions standard with which the EGU must comply; (vi) indication whether P_gross/net used in compliance determinations are based solely on gross electrical load.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no compliance periods end in the quarter include a statement to that effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final quarterly (annual) report additional contents
rubrics_metrics.description: In the final quarterly report of each calendar year include: (i) gross energy output or net energy output sold to an electric grid over the four quarters of the calendar year (as applicable); and (ii) the potential electric output of the EGU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic reporting tool requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You must submit all electronic reports required under paragraph (a) using the Emissions Collection and Monitoring Plan System (ECMPS) Client Tool provided by the Clean Air Markets Division (CAMD).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with Acid Rain Program reporting (subpart G of part 75)
rubrics_metrics.description: For affected EGUs under this subpart that are also subject to the Acid Rain Program, you must meet applicable reporting requirements and submit reports as required under subpart G of part 75; for those not in Acid Rain Program, you must also meet subpart G reporting requirements to the extent they provide applicable data for compliance demonstrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newly-constructed EGUs subject to Acid Rain must begin submitting quarterly electronic emissions reports per 40 CFR 75.64(a) beginning with data recorded on and after the earlier of provisional certification date or 180 days after commercial operation. Newly-constructed EGUs not subject to Acid Rain must begin submitting per 75.64(a) if that date is on or after May 23, 2023. Reconstructed/modified units begin reporting when they become affected under this subpart, provided ECMPS can receive/process net energy output data; otherwise report on gross energy output until Client Tool can receive net output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim reporting when monitoring systems not provisionally certified
rubrics_metrics.description: If any required monitoring system has not been provisionally certified by the date emissions data reporting is required to begin, the maximum (or in some cases, minimum) potential value for the parameter measured shall be reported until certification testing is successfully completed, per 40 CFR 75.4(j), 75.37(b), or section 2.4 of appendix D to part 75.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operating hours in which CO2 mass emission rates are calculated using maximum potential values are not “valid operating hours” and shall not be used in compliance determinations under §60.5540.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report submission authority and designation (Designated Representative)
rubrics_metrics.description: For affected EGUs subject to the Acid Rain Program reports shall be submitted by the Designated Representative (DR), Alternate DR (ADR), or a person authorized by the DR/ADR to make required submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For affected EGUs not subject to Acid Rain the owner/operator shall appoint a DR and optionally an ADR to submit required reports; DR and ADR must register with CAMD Business System. The DR may delegate authority to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and accounting for captured CO2
rubrics_metrics.description: If your affected EGU captures CO2 to meet the emission standard, you must report in accordance with 40 CFR part 98, subpart PP, and either: (1) report under 40 CFR part 98 subpart RR or VV if injection occurs on-site; (2) transfer captured CO2 to a facility that reports under subpart RR or VV if injection off-site; or (3) transfer captured CO2 to a facility that has received an innovative technology waiver from EPA pursuant to paragraph (g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver process for captured CO2 transfer requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may request the Administrator to issue a waiver of the requirement that captured CO2 be transferred to a facility reporting under part 98 subpart RR or VV. To receive a waiver applicant must demonstrate technology will store captured CO2 as effectively as geologic sequestration and not cause unreasonable risk to public health, welfare, or safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrator considers operating history, whether technology increases emissions/releases of pollutants other than CO2, permanence. Administrator may test system or require tests, may grant conditional approval with monitoring/reporting conditions, may withdraw approval on evidence of releases, and will provide public notice of any application and proposed action.

rubrics_metrics.name: General recordkeeping obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: You must maintain records of the information you used to demonstrate compliance with this subpart as specified in §60.7(b) and (f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records must be kept in accordance with additional specific requirements and retention period specified in this subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum recordkeeping items tied to part 75 systems
rubrics_metrics.description: For affected EGUs (Acid Rain and non-Acid Rain) you must at a minimum keep specified records as applicable to the continuous monitoring systems used, including: (i) monitoring plan records under 40 CFR 75.53(g) and (h); (ii) operating parameter records under 75.57(b)(1)-(4); (iii) records under 75.57(c)(2) for stack gas volumetric flow rate; (iv) records under 75.57(c)(3) for continuous moisture monitoring; (v) records under 75.57(e)(1) (except e(1)(x)) for CO2 concentration monitors or O2 monitors used to calculate CO2 concentration; (vi)-(vii) specified oil and gas flow meter records under 75.58; (viii) QA records under 75.59(a)(1)-(12),(15) for CEMS; (ix) QA records under 75.59(b)(1)-(4) for fuel flow meters; (x) records of DAHS verification under 75.59(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping of emission calculation records
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep records of the calculations you performed to determine the hourly and total CO2 mass emissions (tons) for each operating month and each compliance period, including each 12-operating-month compliance period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping of energy output calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep records of the applicable data recorded and calculations performed that you used to determine your affected EGU's gross or net energy output for each operating month.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping of valid-hour percentage calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep records of the calculations you performed to determine the percentage of valid CO2 mass emission rates in each compliance period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping of compliance assessment calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep records of the calculations you performed to assess compliance with each applicable CO2 mass emissions standard in table 1 or 2 to this subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping for site-specific F-factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep records of the calculations you performed to determine any site-specific carbon-based F-factors you used in emissions calculations (if applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping of electric sales for stationary combustion turbines
rubrics_metrics.description: For stationary combustion turbines keep records of electric sales to determine the applicable subcategory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping to demonstrate system emergency operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep records to demonstrate that your affected facility operated during a system emergency, including: (1) documentation that the system emergency was in effect from the issuing entity and exact duration; (2) documentation that the emergency included the affected source/region; and (3) documentation that the affected facility was instructed to increase output beyond planned day-ahead or remain in operation outside scheduled dispatch, from a Reliability Coordinator, Balancing Authority, or Independent System Operator/Regional Transmission Organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention format and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Your records must be in a form suitable and readily available for expeditious review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must maintain each record for 5 years after the date of conclusion of each compliance period.
